content.question: What is the quickest way to duplicate an existing TextView tag in XML?

options.text: Copy (Ctrl-C/Cmd-C) the tag and paste (Ctrl-V/Cmd-V) after it closes
Use the emulator to duplicate it

content.explanation: The instructor demonstrates copying an existing XML tag and pasting it on the next line after its closing bracket to reuse properties quickly.
hints: Place it after the closing > or />

content.question: True or False: If two TextViews are identical and overlap, selecting one and dragging can help reveal which is on top.
content.explanation: Dragging and selecting components in the layout editor makes it possible to move elements and observe which one was overlapping or on top.

content.question: When you paste a copied tag and see squiggly lines underneath, what does the instructor suggest you do first?

options.text: Click the suggestion bulb to inspect errors; if nothing major, ignore for now

content.explanation: The instructor shows that squiggly lines can be non-critical; clicking the suggestion bulb reveals if it's ignorable. If no major issue, it's safe to continue.

content.question: Which shortcut undoes your last action in Android Studio (Windows and Mac)?
content.explanation: Undo is performed with Ctrl-Z on Windows and Cmd-Z on Mac; the instructor uses this to revert deletions and restore attributes.

content.question: Why might a developer ignore some squiggly lines after pasting a tag?

options.text: They are always caused by malware
They can be due to internal configuration warnings that don't prevent building the app
They mean the file is corrupted
They always indicate missing mandatory attributes

content.explanation: Some squiggly lines are non-critical internal warnings; only missing mandatory attributes will typically prevent the app from building.
